claim_text: Two co-primaries, distribution-free, one-sided, at alpha_adj = 1 - 0.95^(1/2) = 0.0253205655 each. Both must pass for the Stage B GO row.
source_of_truth: src/etf/config.py:25 (ALPHA_ADJ = 1.0 - 0.95 ** (1.0/2.0)); reports/stage_a2/power.json alpha_adj; REGISTRATION.md:285-286 and :392-395; src/etf/section0.py:139
recomputed_value: alpha_adj reproduces exactly (0.025320565519103666). Re-running the repository's own functions at the uncorrected alpha=0.05: E1 power at N=163 rises 0.6105 -> 0.7320; E1 minimum N falls 237 -> 207 (and 845 -> 748); E2 power at n=300 rises 0.8000 -> 0.8967 (grid minimum stays 300 at a step of 50). The closure verdict does not move: 163 still falls short of both minimums and E1 stays between the 0.50 and 0.80 floors.
reason: Sidak is a union-type correction controlling P(at least one false rejection); the decision rule it feeds is an all-must-pass conjunction (an intersection-union test), whose size is bounded by the largest component level. Each component may therefore be tested at the full 0.05 with no inflation, and the correction costs power for nothing.
estimator: Sidak per-test alpha for 2 tests at family-wise 0.05
data_structure: two co-primary permutation tests on the same admissible-day sample
notes: T1. DRAFT-V-3. The only disjunctive use of Sidak in the registration - the four-cell threshold-sensitivity secondary at REGISTRATION.md:315-316 - is correct.
